html:
The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565 near the Krishna River in Karnataka. An alliance of the Deccan sultanates destroyed the army of Vijayanagara, and the greatest city of south India was sacked.

Vijayanagara was then run by Rama Raya, regent and father-in-law of the king. For twenty years he had played the sultans of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar against each other and taken land from each. In 1564 the four made peace through marriages and joined forces against him.

The armies were very large. Rama Raya, said to be about eighty, commanded from a litter. The sultans' massed guns, firing bags of copper coins at close range, broke the charge. Two Muslim commanders in Vijayanagara's pay are said to have changed sides. Rama Raya was captured and beheaded on the spot, and his army fled.

The court left with the treasure on 1,500 elephants. The victors then spent about five months looting and burning the capital. The ruins are at Hampi.

The empire lived on from new capitals further south until 1646, much weakened. Its governors, the nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur and Mysore, became kings in their own right.
